final_candidates.decision_summary: Charge reversal at a GP1 epitope residue disrupts antibody binding while likely preserving entry.
Alanine substitution at a surface residue in the same epitope reduces antibody contact with minimal structural impact.
Introducing arginine at a loop position may alter the antibody-recognized conformation and improve escape.

stop_reason.detail: Sufficient candidate quality reached without external evidence; further self-iteration would not meaningfully improve the ranking.

history.rationale: Surface-exposed GP1 residue in a likely antibody-contact loop; charge reversal can disrupt mAb binding while retaining the local backbone context.
Charge reversal at a surface-exposed GP1 residue likely disrupts antibody binding while retaining hydrogen-bonding capacity to preserve function.
Charge-reversal at a key GP1 epitope residue is likely to disrupt antibody binding without severely compromising entry.
GP1 polar residue near a neutralizing epitope and adjacent to the N109 glycan; truncating the side chain removes potential antibody contacts with low structural perturbation.
Alanine substitution removes a potential antibody contact without major structural perturbation; position likely resides in a neutralizing epitope.
Alanine substitution at a surface residue in the same epitope region may reduce antibody contact while preserving core structure.
Aromatic GP1 surface residue likely contacted by neutralizing antibodies; alanine substitution removes the bulky side chain and may reduce affinity without disrupting the fold.
Large aromatic to alanine may destabilize the protein core and compromise cell entry, making it less favorable for improving the phenotype.
Large hydrophobic to alanine may disrupt local packing without clear antibody escape benefit; lower priority than new glycosylation-site mutation.

rejection.reason: Large hydrophobic to alanine may disrupt local packing without clear antibody escape benefit; lower priority than new glycosylation-site mutation.

history.rationale: Small GP1 surface residue in an antigenic stretch; valine introduces a beta-branched steric clash for antibody engagement while preserving a tolerated hydrophobic mutation.
Serine to valine alters side-chain shape and hydrophobicity, likely affecting epitope recognition while being conservative enough to preserve folding.
Hydrophobic substitution may perturb antibody binding while retaining overall fold.
GP1 histidine on a solvent-exposed potential antibody epitope; charge reversal can sterically/electrostatically impair binding without altering the receptor-binding core.
Histidine to aspartate changes charge and hydrogen-bonding pattern, potentially affecting antibody recognition with moderate risk to stability.
Charge change at a nearby epitope residue adds diversity to escape potential.
Exposed GP1 polar residue; introducing a large cationic side chain can block the antibody interface while retaining overall surface compatibility.
Introduction of a positively charged side chain may alter antigenic surface while the polar nature of glutamine to arginine is tolerated in loop regions.
Introducing a charged residue at position 165 could alter the antibody-recognized loop conformation, favoring escape.
GP1 C-terminal surface residue near the GP1/GP2 interface; charge flip can affect a cocktail antibody contact without disturbing the furin-cleavage RRLL motif.
Arginine to glutamate changes charge significantly; may affect antibody binding but could also impact interface stability.
Charge flip may disrupt an antibody contact at the GP1/GP2 interface.
GP2 N-terminal exposed residue in a fusion-proximal antibody contact; conservative removal of the threonine hydroxyl may reduce antibody binding with modest fusion-function risk.
Conservative alanine substitution likely has limited effect on epitope recognition and may be insufficient to achieve escape.
Conservative substitution in GP2; lower priority.
Surface GP2 helical residue likely bound by one cocktail component; charge inversion can impair antibody recognition while maintaining helical propensity.
Charge inversion in GP2 may disrupt epitope for antibodies targeting that region; moderate conservation due to surface location.
Potential contact for neutralizing antibodies in the GP2 fusion subunit; moderate confidence given entry concerns.
GP2 surface loop residue in a potential neutralizing-antibody footprint; charge inversion may disrupt mAb contacts but carries a moderate viability risk.
Charge swap in GP2 might interfere with antibody binding but carries a higher risk of disrupting fusion or trimer contacts.
GP2 mutation with uncertain effect on fusion; kept as backup.
N119 is an N-linked glycosylation site in the GP1 epitope region; removal may disrupt antibody binding while potentially retaining entry.
